name: spn-core
description: SaaS Plane core, stack-agnostic: the DevEx stage skills (check, scm, ideate, plan, develop, test, provision, deliver, operate, report) — including ideate, the interactive loop that decides a boundary and shape into the repo-root CONCEPT.md before anything is planned; the SPN engineer persona; the spn-panel reviewer and the lens files it convenes (lead, business, product, architect, server-dev, web-dev, qa, infra, trust, partner, voice); contract review rules; the command vocabulary; the doc-set rules every node's docs are built to; the cross-repo working protocol; the getting-started restatement; the new-platform intake worksheet; a hook that denies hand-edits to generated files; and a hook that checks every document — seats, READMEs, the concept, the artifacts — against the bars the book states mechanically: audience in the masthead, the Terms bound, no cardinality in prose, and the one voice measured (around fifteen words a sentence, you present; RD.DOCS.043). It also carries refs/permission-vs-enablement.md — the first question an agent asks before declaring a gate: does the answer vary per person, per organization type, or per plan. A SessionStart hook prints the window's orientation — the workspace members read from their own sprepo.json, the law and plugin set each carries, the wiring, every workstream in its own state (backlog, open, closed) with its number, and one open question — and points at the day-zero skill when the workspace holds no repository at all. Two more PreToolUse hooks read a workstream's split plan: the documents-first gate warns when an approach page is written into a repo's pocket while an open workstream still has rows unlanded, and the close gate refuses a move into workstreams/closed/ while any row is one nobody decided — landed, carried and deferred all pass, because the check is accounted for rather than finished. Moving backlog/ into open/ is how work starts, and no gate fires on it. refs/cross-repo.md states when work earns a workstream, and which state you propose a new one starts in. The day-zero skill walks an empty folder to two repositories: the estate questions first, then the acts. refs/cross-repo.md also carries the machine seat, ~/.spnenv — one file for every SaaS Plane value, read directly by spnutils — with the never-render rule (report key names and set-state, never a region), its four marked regions and one writer each (producer, managed, an untouched spnutils:dev, then keep), the rule that spnutils provisions the shape while the agent adds the key and asks for the value, the ${VAR} reference grammar it shares with the cloud secret store, and namespacing by platform code rather than by workspace. It states the producer and partner boundary once: a partner holds no marketplace, blueprint or book checkout, so the book is cited by name and the marketplace source follows the mode the place implies.
